result: WIP at context checkpoint: tracer gives byte-identical trace files on Zen 1, Skylake-SP, Haswell-EP (17/17, was 8/17) via a virtual CPU per class and fixed env; the data-redirection step breaks p_cold (red inside lthc-canon3-mei); regen --build proof, plants, gate not run
head: 699fb8ad1

rulings.item: Trace cost: four CPU-class runs per probe (fast set 126-479 s vs about 60 s)
rulings.recommendation: accept until LT-3's ptrace tracer; classes are the only host-independent way to group every candidate

rulings.item: Residual host inputs the tree cannot carry: localedef/en_US source, /usr/share/locale (alias, catalogs), zone files, kernel, nscache /dev/shm region state
rulings.recommendation: redirect the nscache region path per run (next step); keep the rest as printed digests

informational: Today's cross-host trace differences are CPU class only (ERMS: fill_erms on Intel, not Zen 1); the locale archive, zone file and nsswitch.conf are byte-identical on the three hosts
A user namespace cannot be used to substitute data: nscache.rs keeps a private table there, changing the traced path
lthc-canon3-mei: regen trace-only rc 1 (p_cold stops early under the path redirection); job rc 0 is the wrapper script

impact.what: hot-text trace files byte-identical across Zen 1 / Skylake-SP / Haswell-EP (same products)

improvement: A cross-host trace diff of one set of products (copy products, trace-only) finds host inputs in minutes without any build; worth a tool
next_step: Read lthc-canon3-mei (redirect variant), handle the nscache /dev/shm region, then the 3-host regen --build proof both profiles, plants, record, gate
